title: The 5 Planets With the Longest Days, Ranked (The Sun's Neighbor Is Only #2)

scenes.text: The slowest-spinning planet is not the one closest to the Sun.

scenes.label: Uranus · 17 h 14 min
scenes.text: Number five: Uranus. One spin takes about seventeen hours and fourteen minutes, even though it rolls around on its side.

scenes.label: Earth · 23 h 56 min
scenes.text: Number four: Earth. One spin takes twenty-three hours and fifty-six minutes, measured against the stars.

scenes.label: Mars · 24 h 37 min
scenes.text: Number three: Mars. One spin takes twenty-four hours and thirty-seven minutes, barely longer than ours.

scenes.label: Mercury · 59 Earth days
scenes.text: Number two: Mercury. One full spin takes about fifty-nine Earth days. Closest to the Sun, but not the slowest.

scenes.label: Venus · 243 Earth days
scenes.text: Number one: Venus. One spin takes two hundred forty-three Earth days, longer than its own two hundred twenty-five day year.

description:
The five planets that spin slowest, ranked by the time one full rotation takes.
Mercury is closest to the Sun but only second slowest: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once, which is longer than its year.
Which planet would you least want to live on?
first_comment: Would you rather live on Mercury or Venus? And what should we rank next?
